articleTitle: Evaluation of the Clinical Utility of a Gait Analysis System Using Pose Estimation Techniques in Physical Therapy
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: Conventional observational motion analysis in physical therapy is subject to biases that require a more quantitative approach to gait analysis. This study presents the development of a gait analysis system using pose estimation techniques and explores the usefulness of quantitative gait analysis in clinical rehabilitation. The proposed system employs a PC and a webcam to identify leg joint angles by estimating keypoints using OpenPose. Initially, the system was validated in a laboratory against 3D position measuring equipment, demonstrating promising accuracy, particularly in the estimation of knee joint angles. Next, we examined whether the accuracy of the gait analysis verified in the laboratory was adequate for actual rehabilitation. The validation results revealed a statistically significant difference between the healthy group and the left and right hemiplegic patient groups. The machine learning classification achieved a three-class classification between healthy subjects’ hemiplegic and legs with hemiplegic disease with an accuracy of 80%. The proposed simple motion analysis system, using posture estimation technique contributes to the quantitative evaluation of gait analysis in physical therapy.

articleTitle: Performance Bound for Iterative Learning Control of Iteration-Varying Battery SoC Profiles Under Iteration-Invariant Learning Gains
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: This research studies the problem of learning and control for electric vehicle (EV) battery state-of-charge (SoC) profiles subject to their slight daily variations. These variations are due to many factors including traffic and weather conditions, driver behaviors, etc., hence pose a challenge on how to learn from such small changes on the SoC patterns to derive better control algorithms for the EV batteries. To cope with such challenge, iterative learning control (ILC) framework is employed in the current study, and iteration-invariant learning gains are first used to verify the performance limit induced by such gains. Accordingly, an explicit and analytical upper bound is derived for the ILC tracking error, which shows the effects of the ILC learning gain, the SoC profile variations, and the initial ILC setup.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Resource Allocations in Maritime Port Operations Using Queue Models
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: The main function of maritime container terminal operations is to allow transfer of containers between ships and other types of transportation, such as trucks or trains. These transfer operations are often modelled as dynamic discrete-time system of queues, which are controlled by a set of input variables that relate to the available resources. These variables are functions of the capacities of the equipment that is employed to handle the containers in the terminal. In the present study, an optimal control method is proposed that focuses on the effective allocation of such resources in a maritime container terminal. Therefore, a dynamic discrete-time queue model for container terminal operations is introduced and represented in formal manner. Based on this model, the resource allocation is formulated as an optimisation problem. The obtained simulation result for an abstract container terminal indicate that the proposed optimal control mechanism for resources allocation allows managing maritime terminal operations more effectively.

articleTitle: Passivity-Short-Based Conditions of System-Wide Stability and L2 gain Performance for Heterogeneous Nonlinear Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: The tendency to incorporate heterogeneity in bus dynamics for designing resilient and efficient power system has received increasing attention in recent years. This paper introduces novel passivity-short-based conditions to ensure system-wide stability and guarantee L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gain performance in power system with heterogeneous bus dynamics and nonlinear coupling. At first, we show the decomposition of the power system. By leveraging passivity indices and passivity-short-based property, the proposed framework offers a comprehensive approach to evaluate the system-wide stability of the power system. Additionally, we extend to evaluate L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gain performance via passivity indices, offering insights into the robustness of the power system. A power system simulation with 3 typical bus dynamics is illustrated considering the load change to demonstrate the efficiency of the presented conditions.

articleTitle: Broadband Modeling of Power Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: This paper proposes a modeling and simulation procedure of power distribution networks (PDN) based on polynomial fitting and bilinear transformation to generate datasets for data-driven control of DCDC converters. A measurement setup is proposed which enables the definition of PDN capturing its broadband and high dynamic range characteristics. In order to quantify the modeling error, a method for measuring the required signals and for efficient simulation is proposed. The modeling and simulation procedure is applied to a measured PDN and the modeling error is discussed.

articleTitle: Incentivizing Control Design for Blockchain-Enabled Distributed Optimization in Electricity Market Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: This paper provides an incentivizing control design for blockchain-enabled distributed optimization in electricity market systems. After a wholesale multi-spot bidding problem in electricity market systems is first formulated, an incentivizing distributed optimization inspired by the mechanism design in economics is proposed, and we discuss the relationship between the proposed utility/incentive function design and the potential game. Moreover, it is explained that the proposed mechanism can be implemented on a blockchain system based on Solidity. The effectiveness of the proposed control architecture is finally illustrated by simulation.

articleTitle: Stabilization of hyperbolic reaction-diffusion systems on directed networks through the generalized Routh-Hurwitz criterion for complex polynomials
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: The study of dynamical systems on complex networks is of paramount importance in engineering, given that many natural and artificial systems find a natural embedding on discrete topologies. For instance, power grids, chemical reactors and the brain, to name a few, can be modeled through the network formalism by considering elementary units coupled via the links. In recent years, scholars have developed numerical and theoretical tools to study the stability of those coupled systems when subjected to perturbations. In such framework, it was found that asymmetric couplings enhance the possibilities for such systems to become unstable. Moreover, in this scenario the polynomials whose stability needs to be studied bear complex coefficients, which makes the analysis more difficult. In this work, we put to use a recent extension of the well-known Routh-Hurwitz stability criterion, allowing to treat the complex coefficient case. Then, using the Brusselator model as a case study, we discuss the stability conditions and the regions of parameters when the networked system remains stable.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of Wind Affected Maneuverability of Tugboat-Controlled Ships
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: Maritime transport in narrow canals and crowded harbours has received considerable attention during the past few years due to the incident in the Suez Canal. Maneuvering a large container ship effectively, ensuring safety in a confined space, is a challenging problem. One way of overcoming this challenge is using tugboats in critical areas under the supervision of responsible pilots. These operations pose more challenges under extreme weather conditions and may lead to accidents, monetary losses, and loss of lives. This strongly suggests the need for automated assistant systems. In [1], the maneuverability of tugboat-controlled ships under the influence of wind is investigated by deriving a dynamic model for the ship which takes tugboat and wind forces into account, and calculating critical wind speeds based on this model. This delivers a risk assessment about the maneuverability of a desired maneuver. In this paper, we provide a sensitivity analysis for the work presented in [1] to investigate how the critical wind speeds are influenced by changing environmental situations.

articleTitle: Optimal RTGC Non-linear Control System Based on Sliding Mode Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: The high traffic of containers between countries and continents demands the implementation of automation at cargo seaports. Rubber Tyred Gantry Crane (RTGC) is one of the main components for loading and unloading at container yards which needs to move the container accurately to the desired position and minimize the sway during this process. This paper attempts to examine non-linear control using the sliding mode controller (SMC) method for MIMO control problems in RTGC. The control objective is to reduce the swing angle and move the container to the desired position and height by means of the force of two motors on RTGC. The detailed derivation of the nonlinear RTGC model, the design of SMC and its sliding surface are introduced in this paper. In order to optimize the performance of the SMC control action, the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grid search methods are employed in the investigation. The obtained results demonstrate that the SMC exhibits satisfactory control performance and effectively reduces chattering across various initial conditions and system parameters.

articleTitle: A Non-contact Translational and Rotational Force Feedback Device using Rotational Jet Propellers
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a non-contact, translational and rotational force feedback device using rotational jet propellers. With its location and orientation tracked by an optimized tracking system, the system can exert forces in arbitrary directions regardless of the device’s orientation. This device can provide forces of up to 15N in various directions. By directing the two jet propellers in opposite directions, it can produce not only two degree of freedom translational forces but also one degree of freedom rotational forces. Using three Unity applications, we verified the impact of this device on VR experiences, focusing on three aspects: immersion, realism, and discomfort.

articleTitle: Data-driven Optimal Control with Data Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: This paper presents a data compensation method to obtain the solution of a data-driven approach Lyapunov equation with data loss. By applying this method, the optimal control problems for continuous-time linear systems with partially known parameters can be solved with limited data information. A numerical simulation is performed to demonstrate the solution.

articleTitle: State space analysis of the relation between two types of disturbance observers
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: This paper analyzes the structures and the internal dynamic characteristics of two types of disturbance observers. The disturbance observer is used to estimate and compensate the disturbance and the variation of the inputs caused by uncertainties. The exosystem-model-based disturbance observer is constructed against the augmented system with the disturbance generating model and the nominal plant model (Johnson (1972)). There is also the inverse-model-based disturbance observer, which is constructed with the inverse model of the nominal plant model (Ohishi et al. (1983)). The differences and advantages between these two types of disturbance observers have yet to be fully understood. Accordingly, this paper aims to clarify the relation between two types of disturbance observers from the viewpoint of state-space representation. First, the paper shows the explicit realization of the inverse-model-based disturbance observer. Then, a detailed analysis of the relation between the inverse-model-based and exosystem-model-based disturbance observers is given. This analysis shows the correspondence between the observer gains and the dynamics of the disturbance generating model.

articleTitle: Localization Fault Detection Method using 2D LiDAR and Fisheye Camera for an Autonomous Mobile Robot Control
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: Localization is an important function of autonomous mobile robots, and autonomous actions caused by incorrectly estimated robot posture may lead to major accidents. In this study, we propose a fault detection function of localization using 2D LiDAR and fisheye camera. The proposed fault detection method focuses on the likelihood to detect faults, which can be improved by suppressing the update of the particle filter based localization. We conducted several experiments in real environments to verify the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Reduced-order H∞ Filter Synthesis of Discrete-time Uncertain Switched Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: It deals with event-triggered reduced-order H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> filter synthesis of discrete-time uncertain switched systems. It is considered norm-bounded uncertainties affecting the uncertain switched systems’ behavior. An event-triggered strategy is firstly specified to identify whether information of the uncertain switched system is transmitted or not. Then, a reduced-order H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> filter is designed ground on outputs of the proposed event-triggered strategy. And utilizing the merging switching signal technique, a switched filtering error system is modeled by the uncertain switched system and reduced-order H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> filter. Subsequently, some sufficient critera are presented to guarantee that the switched filtering error system is exponentially stable with a weighted H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance. A design method is also given for the reduced-order H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> filter. Finally, the validity and feasibility of this study is illustrated by a practical example.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Dynamic Behavior of a Both-Sides Retrodirective System for the Control of Microwave Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: Long distance wireless power transfer is achieved by large antenna systems which employ a number of antenna elements. The larger the antenna, the longer the distance that can be achieved. To maximize the power transfer, the amplitude and phase of each antenna element must be controlled precisely according to the values that are predicted by an S-parameter view. Iterative approaches to control them are considered to compensate for the time-varying behavior of the wireless channel but these methods rapidly increase in computational complexity as the system grows in size. The use of retrodirective antenna arrays on both the power generator antennas and the receiver antennas have been proposed as an alternative. The feedback looping mechanism of this method enables a highly efficient power transfer. In this paper, we analyze the dynamic behavior of this proposed system in terms of its zero-input response and step response. We show that at marginal stability, the proposed system can achieve maximum theoretical efficiency. The theoretical analysis is validated by a time-domain simulation and results show agreement with theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Towards a Safer Built Environment Industry with Inverted Perching Aerial Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: This paper presents an inverted perching mechanism designed for an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) intended for fluid spraying applications in the construction industry. The perching mechanism incorporates rotary and prismatic joints, enabling the UAV to change its body orientation while in a perched state. To ensure the effective operation of the inverted perching approach, several challenges including impact absorption, thrust control, and UAV body rotation need to be addressed. To tackle these challenges, the paper proposes the utilization of a Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC) thrust controller and an optimization-based UAV positioning strategy. The combined operation of these control strategies with the perching mechanism improves the UAV’s ceiling approach performance. Simulation and experimentation results demonstrate a relative increase in ±5° body rotation capability and a notable 17.65% improvement in impact absorption.

articleTitle: Scalar Modules with Logarithmic Lyapunov Functions for Robust Positive Systems Exhibiting Interior Equilibria
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: This paper pursues the use of logarithmic functions to develop a dissipativity framework for module-based analysis and design of nonlinear dynamical systems evolving on positive orthants and having interior stationary points. For scalar module systems, the notion of asymmetric supply rate and asymmetric gain is formulated for establishing input-to-state stability (ISS) with positivity through the logarithmic storage functions. In contrast to systems without state space restrictions, targeting interior equilibria prevents asymptotic stability from implying ISS for additive perturbations. The tightness of the asymmetric supply rate is investigated by clarifying the involvement of the equilibria information.

articleTitle: Interception of Multiple Drone Targets by Heterogeneous Chasers using Heuristic Task Allocations with DQN-GNN Guidance Model
publicationTitle: 2024 SICE International Symposium on Control Systems (SICE ISCS)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of air-to-air drone interception for counter-UAS operations. The fleet of interceptors (agents) are assigned to intercept the intruders (targets) mid air at designated area. There is requirement for heuristic task allocation algorithm to assign each of the agent to track and look for specific target, for better chasing (intervention) effectiveness and better use of resources, especially in cases of heterogeneous (non-identical) chasing agents. The task allocation framework is modelled as matching and optimization problem and based on the weapon target assignment problem. The preliminary mix-integer, non-linear problem (MINLP) formulations are based on probability of interception, resource readiness and threat evaluation are used. After which, the individual agent path planning path will be done through deep Q-network with Graph Neural Network (DQN-GNN) reinforcement neural network. This learning based approach provide the guidance rules and allows the assigned agents to track the target in any environment including existing obstacles and other moving objects. Preliminary works have shown that the combination of the proposed heuristic task allocation and the Deep Q-network with Graph Neural Network (DQN-GNN) framework help more successful interception in specific time frames.

Author Keywords: Deep Q-network with Graph Neural Network (DQN-GNN)
